chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Baseer, and Bureyd al-Ijli, and al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding the cows: in every thirty cows, one Tabi' (one-year-old cow) is due, and there is nothing due for less than that; and in forty cows, one Musinnah (two-year-old cow) is due, and there is nothing due for what is between thirty and forty until it reaches forty. So when it reaches forty, then in it is one Musinnah, and there is nothing due for what is between forty and sixty. So when it reaches sixty, then in it are two Tabi' up to seventy. So when it reaches seventy, then in it is one Tabi' and one Musinnah up to eighty. So when it reaches eighty, then in every forty is one Musinnah up to ninety. So when it reaches ninety, then in it are three Tabi' (one-year-olds). So when it reaches one hundred and twenty, then in every forty is one Musinnah.

Then the cows are accounted for according to their ages. And there is nothing due on the 'Nayyif' (extra ten), nor on the fractions, nor on the 'Awilah' (working cows). Indeed, the Zakat is on the grazing herd. And whatever has not completed a year in the possession of its owner, there is nothing due upon it until the year passes over it. So when the year passes over it, it becomes obligatory upon it.
ai.seo_question: What is the Zakat rate for cattle according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the detailed nisab and distribution rules for Zakat on cattle, emphasizing that the obligation applies specifically to 'saimah' (grazing herds) rather than working animals. It highlights the Shia scholarly principle that the lunar year (hawl) must be completed in the owner's possession for the tax to become due, excluding fractional counts or non-grazing livestock.
